title: Stapleton: dead faith fictive for perfect justice, not fictive as to faith's own virtue
source_text: X. Et eodem modo Stapletonus concedit fidem mortuam & informem dici posse fictam & hypocriticam, quantum ad justitiae vitam & veritatem spectat. Est autem, inquit, haec fides sine charitate mortua quidem, & ficta seu hypocritica, quantum ad perfectae justitiae vitam & veritatem spectat, non autem quantum ad seipsam, sibique propriam virtutem. De Justif. lib. 8. cap. 9.
pass_a_gloss: And in the same way Stapleton concedes that dead and unformed faith can be called feigned and hypocritical as far as concerns the life and truth of justice. But this faith without charity, he says, is indeed dead, and feigned or hypocritical, as far as concerns the life and truth of perfect justice, yet not as far as concerns itself and the virtue proper to it. On Justification, book 8, chapter 9.
pass_b_english: Stapleton likewise: dead, unformed faith may be called feigned or hypocritical with respect to the life and truth of perfect justice.
It is not feigned with respect to faith itself and the virtue proper to faith.

lemmas.gloss: as far as concerns the life and truth of justice
and the virtue proper to itself

rejected: dead faith is nothing but hypocrisy
